sections.Astrophysical Alerts:
#### M87: LHAASO-WCDA measures a strong multi-day TeV flare

LHAASO reported on **19 November 2026 at 04:02 UTC** that its WCDA blind-search monitor flagged very-high-energy emission from **M87** on **16 November** with **TS = 119** in a two-day integration. A dedicated daily analysis finds enhanced emission from **15–17 November**, peaking on 16 November at **TS = 92.7 (about 9.6σ)**; the three-day stack gives **TS = 122 (about 11σ)** at a position consistent with M87. The preliminary 0.5–20 TeV intrinsic spectrum is a power law with photon index **1.68 ± 0.29**, with statistical uncertainty only. The integral flux above 1 TeV is about **0.5 Crab**, roughly seven times the 1 October–14 November baseline, and the signal remains significant to about **15 TeV**. [LHAASO alert](https://www.astronomerstelegram.org/?read=18161).

This is a high-significance flare from a known variable TeV radio galaxy, not a new source association. The spectrum and flux are preliminary, the quoted index excludes systematic uncertainty, and the telegram reports no significant cutoff rather than proving that none exists. Contemporaneous imaging and multiwavelength data are needed to locate the emitting zone within M87's unresolved TeV source region.

#### 3C 138: MAGIC reports the first VHE detection of a compact steep-spectrum quasar

MAGIC reported on **18 November at 18:02 UTC** that observations on the nights of **16 and 17 November** detected the compact steep-spectrum quasar **3C 138** at about **9σ** after **3.4 h**. The average flux above 100 GeV was about **8% of the Crab Nebula flux**. A hint on 16 November prompted a target-of-opportunity observation on 17 November, which established the reported signal. The source position is **RA 80.292°, Dec +16.639° (J2000)** and its redshift is **z = 0.759**. [MAGIC alert](https://www.astronomerstelegram.org/?read=18159).

The collaboration describes this as the first VHE detection of 3C 138 and of the compact steep-spectrum quasar class. That is a preliminary rapid-report claim: no spectrum, energy-dependent significance, trials accounting or systematic uncertainty is supplied, and the LST-1 data were still awaiting a combined analysis. The result establishes an observational target for follow-up; it does not by itself identify the emitting zone or show that compact steep-spectrum quasars form a general VHE population.

#### EP261115a: FXT narrows the position and measures the fading X-ray spectrum

Einstein Probe issued a refined FXT analysis on **18 November at 11:01 UTC** for the transient first detected by WXT at **2026-11-15 00:22:13 UTC**. FXT began its autonomous follow-up at **00:25:52 UTC**, 295 s after the trigger, and observed for **3477 s**. It found an uncatalogued source at **RA 58.6230°, Dec −44.2932° (J2000)** with a **10-arcsec radius uncertainty at 90% confidence**, inside the WXT region. [Refined FXT analysis](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46316); [event thread](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/events/ep261115a).

An absorbed power law gives Galactic hydrogen column density **1.20⁺¹·¹⁴₋₁·₀₃ × 10²¹ cm⁻²**, photon index **2.01⁺⁰·³⁹₋₀·³⁵**, and average unabsorbed 0.5–10 keV flux **5.73⁺⁰·⁷⁶₋₀·⁵⁷ × 10⁻¹² erg s⁻¹ cm⁻²**; all intervals are 90%. This substantially improves the position and adds an X-ray spectrum, but the telegram does not provide a secure optical counterpart, distance or physical classification. The refined result therefore characterizes a fading X-ray transient without establishing its nature.

#### GRB 261118A: Fermi/GBM identifies a likely short burst with a broad localization

Fermi/GBM triggered at **2026-11-18 13:17:49 UTC** and issued its final real-time localization at **13:28 UTC**. The team classifies **GRB 261118A** as a **likely short GRB** and reports **RA 172.9°, Dec +51.0° (J2000)** with a **7.7° statistical uncertainty**. The event was 165° from the LAT boresight. [GBM circular](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46317); [public trigger record](https://gcn.gsfc.nasa.gov/gcn/fermi_grbs.html).

The circular supplies no duration, spectrum, fluence, false-alarm rate or independent counterpart. “Likely short” is therefore the GBM team's prompt classification, not a secure progenitor identification. The broad statistical region also requires the HEALPix map, including the estimated localization systematic, for quantitative follow-up.

#### GRB 261118B: GBM upgrades the earlier candidate to a likely long burst

The Fermi trigger at **2026-11-18 01:50:36.86 UTC**, previously reported only as a broad candidate, received a final localization and **likely long-GRB** classification on **18 November at 17:23 UTC**. GBM places **GRB 261118B** at **RA 272.2°, Dec +60.7° (J2000)** with a **14.7° statistical uncertainty**; it was 14° from the LAT boresight. [Final GBM localization](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46319); [public trigger record](https://gcn.gsfc.nasa.gov/gcn/fermi_grbs.html).

The new circular resolves the prompt pipeline's earlier ambiguity between a GRB and Cyg X-1, but it gives no duration, spectrum, fluence, LAT counterpart or false-alarm probability. The long-burst label remains a preliminary instrument classification, and the very broad localization prevents a unique source association.

#### GRB 261113B: Fermi/GBM adds prompt spectral parameters and fluence

Fermi/GBM reported on **18 November at 20:47 UTC** its analysis of the burst at **2026-11-13 19:45:55.10 UTC**, already detected by Insight-HXMT/HE, GECAM-B and SVOM/GRM. GBM measures a single episode with **T90 ≈ 17.7 s** in 50–300 keV. From T0−5.9 to T0+5.4 s, a cutoff power law gives index **−0.54 ± 0.05** and **Epeak = 212 ± 7 keV**. The 10–1000 keV fluence over that fit interval is **(6.0 ± 0.1) × 10⁻⁶ erg cm⁻²**, and the 1-s peak photon flux from T0+0.6 s is **8.4 ± 0.8 ph s⁻¹ cm⁻²**. [Fermi/GBM analysis](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46320); [event thread](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/events/grb-261113b).

The on-ground GBM region is consistent with the possible SVOM/GWAC optical counterpart, but positional consistency is not proof of association. The spectrum is preliminary, and its integration interval is shorter than the quoted T90. These data strengthen the prompt GRB characterization and complement the earlier off-axis SVOM/GRM measurement; final catalog calibration may change the parameters.

#### V488 Sge: Chandra finds a line-dominated, variable nova spectrum; a cited-reference error was corrected

Chandra observed the active nova **V488 Sge** for about **14 ks on 10 November** and **13 ks on 11 November**; the analysis was reported on **18 November at 16:08 UTC**. The first-order 0.2–10 keV count rate was **1.058 ± 0.0127 counts s⁻¹** on 10 November and **0.920 ± 0.0115 counts s⁻¹** on 11 November. The first exposure included a **2500-s flare**, while the second also showed strong irregular variability. The spectrum is dominated by thermal-plasma emission lines, including H-like and He-like oxygen and nitrogen, with several radiative-recombination continua and little continuum flux. [Chandra report](https://www.astronomerstelegram.org/?read=18158).

The authors state that the data rule out the previously hypothesized **40 eV blackbody-like atmospheric component**. A correction issued on **19 November at 01:38 UTC** clarifies that this hypothesis came from the earlier XMM-Newton report, **ATel 18135**, rather than ATel 18138 as first written. [Correction](https://www.astronomerstelegram.org/?read=18160); [XMM-Newton report](https://www.astronomerstelegram.org/?read=18135). The telegram provides count rates and qualitative spectral identifications, but no plasma-temperature fit, line fluxes or confidence interval for the rejected continuum component; its physical interpretation remains preliminary.
